NeoGas

More function from the same biomass system

Cellulosic performance materials for anaerobic digestion. NeoGas is being developed from agricultural residues for evaluation as a low-dose additive in anaerobic digestion and biomethane production.

Pilot validation in preparation

Material architecture under investigation

NeoNaar is developing its own cellulosic and lignocellulosic material architecture through controlled processing. The programme explores how material state relates to microbial conversion and methane-production behaviour.

  • Cellulose accessibility
  • Residual lignin and retained hemicellulose
  • Hydrated fibre structure and fibrillation level
  • Microbial interaction
  • Methane-production kinetics

Potential functions under evaluation

Hydrolysis support

Investigate whether accessible hydrated cellulose structures can support biological conversion and substrate breakdown.

Microbial-supporting surface

Evaluate fibrillar structures for microbial attachment and biomass retention.

Process consistency

Study a controlled renewable input alongside variable organic feedstocks.

Methane productivity

Determine whether low-dose materials can increase methane-production rate or total productivity relative to untreated digester systems. This outcome has not yet been established.

Designed for evaluation as a biomethane productivity enhancer

NeoGas is under development for methane-productivity and anaerobic-digestion applications. No methane-yield increase, dosage recommendation or commercial performance guarantee is claimed.

Run a controlled evaluation

NeoNaar is working with technology and research partners to evaluate materials under controlled biomethane-production conditions. We are seeking CBG plant operators, anaerobic-digestion laboratories, EPC and process-technology companies, biological-treatment specialists and industrial pilot partners.
